subject: MODELLING OF HIERARCHICAL DATA IN INLA

messages.subject: MODELLING OF HIERARCHICAL DATA IN INLA
parts:
Hello INLA users,
I am still learning how to use INLA. I want to model hierarchical dataset with binary outcome (perinatal mortality) with household and clusters being the source of random effect. However, I want to use prior knowledge I have that perinatal mortality is 41.6 deaths per 1000 live births. I also want to use conjugate beta hyper prior. Now I have this model:
r = inla(perinatal ~ BMI+Bord+Birthint+
           f(V001,model='iid',
             hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "logitbeta", param = c(42.6, 959.4)))) +
           f(V002,model='iid',
             hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "logitbeta", param = c(42.6, 959.4)))), 
         data=mydata,
         weights=mydata$weight,
         control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 1, prec = 1), 
         family = "binomial",
         control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"), 
         control.family = list(
           control.link = list(
             model = "logit",
             a=1.0)), 
         Ntrials = 1,
         verbose = TRUE)
for(a in seq(0.99, 0.01, len=10)) {
  r$.args$control.family[[1]]$control.link$a = a
  r = inla.rerun(r)
The problem which I need to be assisted is wether I have correctly expressed my hyper-priors.
Your help will be highly appreciated
